Panning in music is the distribution of sounds between the left and right channels of a stereo recording. It lets you place instruments at different points in the sound space: for example, the guitar slightly to the left, the keyboards to the right, and the bass and drums closer to the center. This helps each instrument find its own place in the mix and makes the sound more spacious and easier to distinguish. Panning doesn't change the sound of the instrument itself; it only determines where the listener perceives it as coming from.
